chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 104 — Your Names Are Written in Heaven
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. No surviving Aramaic manuscript preserves wording from Chapter 104. The fourth-century Chester Beatty–Michigan Papyrus XII governs all wording it preserves throughout the chapter. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann’s 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, printed pages 89–90, fills physical or textually damaged places in the Greek papyrus and confirms the complete thirteen-verse sequence. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, no commentary was used as Scripture, and no text absent from these primary witnesses was supplied.

verses.text: I swear to you, the righteous, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One, and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.
verses.study: The righteous may be erased from earthly notice, but heavenly messengers remember them and their names stand before the divine glory.
crossReferences: Malachi 3:16 — a book of remembrance is written before the Lord
Luke 10:20 — rejoice that your names are written in heaven

verses.text: Have hope, for at first you were put to shame through evil and distress; but now you will shine like the lights of heaven. You will shine and be seen, and the gates of heaven will be opened to you.
verses.study: Public shame and distress yield to light, visibility, and welcome. The opened heavenly gates signal that the righteous are neither excluded nor forgotten.
crossReferences: Daniel 12:3 — the wise shine like the brightness of heaven
Revelation 3:8 — an opened door is set before the faithful

verses.text: Keep crying out for judgment, and it will appear for you; for all your distress will be required from the rulers and from everyone who helped those who plundered you.
verses.study: The victims’ appeal is not futile. Judgment calls both direct oppressors and the authorities who assisted them to account.
crossReferences: Luke 18:7–8 — God brings justice for those who cry to him
James 5:4 — the cries of defrauded laborers reach the Lord

verses.text: Have hope, and do not abandon your hope, for you will have great joy like the angels of heaven.
verses.study: Hope is grounded in the promised sharing of heavenly joy, not in a denial of the suffering that preceded it.
crossReferences: Psalm 16:11 — fullness of joy is found in God’s presence
Hebrews 10:35 — confidence must not be thrown away because it carries reward

verses.text: Whatever you have had to do, you will not need to hide on the day of great judgment, and you will not be found as sinners. Eternal judgment will remain far from you through every generation of the world.
verses.study: The righteous need not seek concealment when the record is opened. The judgment that exposes sinners confirms rather than condemns their faithful course.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:5–6 — sinners do not stand in judgment, but the righteous are known
1 John 2:28 — the faithful may have confidence rather than shrink away at his appearing

verses.text: Now do not fear, you righteous, when you see sinners growing strong and prospering in their desires. Do not become their companions, but keep far from their violence, for you are destined to become companions of heaven’s host.
verses.study: Visible success must not entice the righteous into partnership with violence. Their true fellowship is with the heavenly assembly.
crossReferences: Psalm 37:1–9 — do not envy evildoers who seem to prosper
Ephesians 5:11 — take no part in fruitless works of darkness

verses.text: Although you sinners say, ‘None of our sins will be investigated or written down,’ your sins are being written down every day.
verses.study: Denial cannot suspend the record. The daily inscription of sin reveals continuous moral accountability beneath apparent impunity.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 17:1 — sin is written with an iron stylus
Revelation 20:12 — the dead are judged from what is written in the books

verses.text: Now I show you that light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins.
verses.study: Every setting in which people act becomes a witness. Neither darkness nor the passage of time makes wrongdoing invisible.
crossReferences: Psalm 139:11–12 — darkness is not dark before God
Job 34:21–22 — no deep darkness can hide those who practice evil

verses.text: Do not be godless in your hearts, and do not lie or alter a word of truth. Do not accuse the word of the Holy and Great One of being false, and do not honor your idols; for all your lies and all your godlessness lead not to righteousness but to great sin.
verses.study: Inner rebellion becomes verbal distortion and false worship. Truthful reception of the holy word cannot be joined to honoring fabricated gods.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 4:2 — the commanded word must not be added to or diminished
Romans 1:25 — exchanging divine truth for a lie leads to false worship

verses.text: Now I know this mystery: sinners will alter and distort words of truth. They will speak evil words, lie, invent great fabrications, and write books in their own words.
verses.study: Enoch foresees not only casual falsehood but the deliberate production of authoritative-looking distortions. Written form does not make a lie true.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 8:8–9 — the lying pen of scribes can falsify instruction
2 Peter 3:16 — unstable people distort sacred writings to their own ruin

verses.text: But if they write all my words truthfully in their own languages, neither altering nor reducing my words, but writing everything truthfully—all that I testified about them from the beginning—
verses.study: Faithful transmission may cross languages while preserving the testimony without distortion or omission. Truthfulness, not one exclusive tongue, is the stated standard.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 31:24–26 — the completed written testimony is preserved as a witness
Revelation 22:18–19 — the prophetic words must not be added to or taken away

verses.text: I know another mystery: the books will be given to the righteous and the wise for joy, truth, and abundant wisdom.
verses.study: The same medium sinners misuse is entrusted to the wise as a gift. True books become instruments of joy, uprightness, and growing wisdom.
crossReferences: Daniel 12:4, 10 — a sealed book is kept for those who will understand
2 Timothy 3:15–17 — sacred writings impart wisdom and equip faithful readers

verses.text: The books will be given to them, and they will believe them and rejoice in them. All the righteous who learned from them every path of truth will receive their reward.
verses.study: The chapter closes with a community receiving, trusting, rejoicing in, and learning from preserved testimony. Knowledge bears fruit as a practiced path of truth.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:7–11 — true instruction gives joy, wisdom, and great reward
James 1:22–25 — the blessed hearer continues in and acts upon the word

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 104 continues the answer to the oppressed righteous. Their names are written before the Great One, angels remember them for good, and heaven’s gates will open to them. The chapter turns the language of heavenly record into personal assurance: forgotten people remain individually known.

This hope requires moral separation in the present. The apparent prosperity of sinners must not draw the righteous into companionship with violence, because their promised fellowship is with heaven’s host. They can continue crying for judgment, confident that rulers and accomplices as well as direct plunderers will be called to account.

The chapter contrasts two kinds of writing. Every sin is recorded despite sinners’ denial, while sinners themselves produce writings that alter truth and dignify invention. Light, darkness, day, and night all witness what people do; concealment and confident assertion cannot turn falsehood into righteousness.

Yet writing is not rejected. When Enoch’s testimony is transmitted truthfully across languages without alteration or reduction, books become gifts of joy, truth, and wisdom. The righteous receive them, believe them, rejoice in them, and learn the paths of truth. The theological center is faithful witness: heaven records truly, judgment uncovers truly, and earthly scribes are charged to transmit truly.

crossReferences: 1 Enoch 103:1–4 — heavenly tablets preserve the reward and remembrance of the righteous
1 Enoch 105:1–2 — God and his Son join themselves to the faithful
Psalm 37:1–20 — apparent wicked prosperity must not displace hope
Psalm 56:8 — suffering and tears are kept in God’s record
Daniel 12:1–4 — the written, delivered, and shining righteous appear together
Malachi 3:16–18 — the book of remembrance distinguishes those who serve God
Luke 10:20 — heavenly citizenship is expressed through written names
2 Timothy 3:14–17 — sacred writings give wisdom and shape faithful practice
2 Peter 3:14–18 — believers resist distortion and remain steadfast
Revelation 20:11–15 — written records are opened in final judgment
